messages:
Alex: heads-up — noticed a perf cliff when routing seq_len ~48 on H100; Triton picks kernel A, CUTLASS would have been faster for that stripe.
Priya: can you paste the profiler snippet?
Alex: pasted below from perf-bot run:
```
seq=48 model=redwood-13B kernel=TritonA latency_p50=42ms p95=120ms offload=0.7
seq=48 model=redwood-13B kernel=CUTLASS_fast latency_p50=30ms p95=60ms offload=0.2
```
Alex: seems like our kernel decider is biased toward TritonA for seq <=64 because of historical p50 on mixed loads.
Mateo: is the KV cache hit pattern different at 48? that can change memory pressure and kernel choice.
Alex: KV hit rate was 0.82 for that workload. Not great but not catastrophic.
Lin: interesting — CUTLASS has better small-seqlen packed matmul for this model variant. Triton wins when seqlen >=128 or when KV coldstart involves big allocations.
Priya: did we see batch-size effects? TritonA benefits from batching more aggressively in our autotuner.
Alex: yes — at batch 8 Triton p50 drops to 28ms, but in production most requests were B=1-4 due to PLG traffic.
Sam: so two levers: (1) routing heuristics that consider seqlen x batch distribution, (2) a fallback probe that can flip to CUTLASS for narrowband traffic.
Mateo: propose additive metric: weighted_cost = alpha*latency_p95 + beta*token_cost + gamma*kv_mem_pressure. We can sweep alpha to prefer CUTLASS for low-batch narrow seqlen.
Priya: +1. Also consider hysteresis window to avoid oscillation when load fluctuates between 1 and 8. E.g., require 5min sustained improvement before switching.
Alex: perf-bot ran a targeted canary: flipped 10% of traffic with seq<=64 & batch<=4 to CUTLASS. Results: 10% buckets saw 18% lower p95, overall tail reduced by 6%.
perf-bot: canary-report: 
- scope: seq<=64,batch<=4,ratio=0.1
- metric: p95 latency drop 18% (stat sig)
- regressions: none at request error rate level
infra-bot: FYI — memory utilization for CUTLASS nodes rose ~3%, within margin.
Lin: that's promising. Need to update kernel-selection matrix: add rule 'if seqlen<=64 and batch<=4 and kv_hit>=0.7 -> prefer CUTLASS_fast' with a probe fallback to Triton after 10% of requests hit timeout.
Sam: how do we implement probe without causing cold-start noise? We should warm CUTLASS VM pools with a small synthetic prefix cache to avoid first-request latency spike.
Mateo: also add rolling probe that samples a user-key hash shard instead of pure random to preserve per-user affinity.
Priya: important: extend telemetry to include per-path kv_cache_evictions and allocator stall time. Those correlate with Triton regressions.
Alex: created an experiment checklist in the repo and linked it in thread: https://internal/redwood/experiments/kernel-narrowband-2026
Sam: can we schedule a short rollback window if we see error patterns? I suggest 30m auto-rollback on 2x error-rate or 3x tail-increase.
Lin: agree. Also add metric for 'switch-regret' — count requests that switched kernel mid-token due to fallback and measure their latency penalty.
Alex: thanks — I'll draft the routing PR with the conditional rule + 10% controlled canary + warmup hooks. Assigning to @Priya for review.
Priya: on it. I'll add the hysteresis and logging for switch events.
Mateo: if you want I can run a broader simulation that replays traffic histograms to tune alpha/beta/gamma.
Alex: please do. Target to ship canary next Tue. :rocket: 
Sam: quick note — avoid using simple p50 as decision input; use a composite of p95 + median cost to capture tail behavior.
Alex: agreed. thanks everyone.
Priya: ping me when the PR is up, I'll run the canary checklist and approve. :thumbsup:
